codeReview.summary: Feature successfully enabled prefix caching and config tuning on top of FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode. No Python code changes — purely operational/documentation. All four validation assertions pass: VAL-GRAPH-004 (100/100 stability test at 4 concurrent users), VAL-GRAPH-005 (TTFT ratio 0.009 << 0.80 threshold), VAL-GRAPH-006 (VRAM usage 93.2% with max-model-len 32768), VAL-GRAPH-007 (478.10 tok/s vs 411.87 baseline = +16.1% at c2). The launch-config-tuned.sh script is comprehensive, includes proper background daemonization, health check loop, and timeout handling. Stability test data confirms 100/100 requests successful with aggregate throughput 276.22 tok/s at c4. Benchmark data and documentation are consistent.

issues.description: The prefix caching test first request TTFT is 15622.99ms — this is anomalously high and likely includes HIP graph warmup time for a cold-start server, not just TTFT. This inflates the TTFT ratio improvement. For a fair comparison of prefix caching benefit, the test should have included a warm-up request (or multiple requests) before measuring TTFT ratios. The 137ms second-request TTFT is genuine, but the 15s first request artificially inflates the ratio to 0.009 (vs a fair comparison that would still pass the 0.80 threshold, just less dramatically). This is non-blocking because the assertion is met, but the measurement methodology could be misleading.

The config_tuned_c2.json benchmark only runs 20 requests (10 per user, 2 users). This is a smaller sample than the baseline runs (which used vllm bench serve with 100+ prompts). The worker compared this coding agent benchmark (478.10 tok/s, 2-user) against the baseline vllm bench serve output (411.87 tok/s). Comparing different benchmark tools could introduce noise. The assertion is still met since both show improvement, but the comparison methodology is mixed.

The launch-config-tuned.sh health check loop uses a MAX_WAIT of 120 seconds, but HIP graph startup takes ~100 seconds. This leaves only a 20-second buffer. For production use, especially with slower machines or larger models, this buffer may be insufficient. Consider increasing to 180 seconds or making it configurable.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The graph-mode-results.md has been updated to include Config-Tuned Mode results, including prefix caching and VRAM data. This is well documented. One gap: the stability test results (276.22 aggregate tok/s at c4) are in the JSON file but not summarized in graph-mode-results.md. Only the stability pass/fail is mentioned, not the throughput at c4.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: graph-mode-results.md: 'Stability Test: 100 requests at 4 concurrent users: 100/100 passed'. stability_test_config_tuned.json shows aggregate_decode_tok_per_s: 276.22.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The health check timeout (120s) is documented in the launch script but not in environment.md. Future workers starting servers need to know that HIP graph mode takes ~100s to start (vs ~60s for eager mode). This is relevant for CI/CD and service health check configuration.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: graph-mode-results.md: 'Total initialization time: ~100 seconds'. launch-config-tuned.sh: MAX_WAIT=120.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The launch-config-tuned.sh creates a background server but does not add this as a named service variant to .factory/services.yaml. Workers wanting to start the config-tuned vLLM server must discover the script manually. A service entry or command like 'start-config-tuned' in services.yaml would make this more discoverable.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: services.yaml only has one vllm service entry (generic). launch-config-tuned.sh exists but is not referenced in services.yaml.

summary: PASS. The prefix-caching-and-config-tuning feature correctly enabled all config optimizations and validated all four assertions (VAL-GRAPH-004 through VAL-GRAPH-007). Three non-blocking issues: (1) prefix caching TTFT measurement conflates cold-start graph warmup with caching benefit; (2) VAL-GRAPH-007 compares different benchmark tools (coding_agent vs vllm bench serve); (3) health check timeout (120s) has only 20s buffer above actual startup time (~100s). Shared state gaps: stability test throughput (276 tok/s at c4) and the launch-config-tuned.sh service should be documented/registered.
